Given data:
- Weight of body $W = 300\text{ N}$
- Inclination of plane $\theta = 60^{\circ}$
- Coefficient of friction $\mu = 0.3$
- Distance travelled $s = 15\text{ m}$

**1. Force required to pull the body up ($P$):**
For motion up the inclined plane:
$$P = W(\sin\theta + \mu \cos\theta)$$
$$P = 300 \left(\sin(60^{\circ}) + 0.3 \cos(60^{\circ})\right)$$
$$P = 300 \left(0.866 + 0.3 \times 0.5\right)$$
$$P = 300 (0.866 + 0.15) = 300 (1.016) = 304.8\text{ N}$|

**2. Work done on the body:**
$$\text{Work Done} = \text{Force along the plane} \times \text{Distance}$$
$$\text{Work Done} = P \times s = 304.8\text{ N} \times 15\text{ m} = 4572\text{ Joules (or N}\cdot\text{m)}$$
proTip: Remember that the pulling force must overcome both the component of gravity down the incline and the frictional resistance.
